prompt: Complete the Dog class so it extends Animal: pass the name to the superclass constructor, override speak() to return "Woof!", and add a fetch() method.
explanation: A subclass calls super(...) in its constructor to hand data to the superclass, which owns the private name field. Overriding speak() replaces the inherited behavior, and dynamic dispatch means the override runs even when the object is held in an Animal variable. New methods like fetch() can freely use inherited public methods such as getName().
hints: The Animal constructor already stores the name. Inside Dog's constructor, call super(name) so the real name gets stored.
To override, declare a method with the exact same signature as in Animal: public String speak(). The @Override annotation lets the compiler check you got it right.
The name field is private to Animal, so fetch() should build its string with the inherited getName() method.
